# function: render_meraki_model

Processes a Meraki Network as Code model and applies network and device templates. YAML strings and the HCL model are merged first, then for every network (`meraki.domains[].organizations[].networks[]`) the templates listed in `templates` are looked up in `meraki.templates.networks`, rendered and merged in list order, with the network's own configuration taking precedence. Afterwards the same is done for every device of every network (`networks[].devices[]`, including devices added by network templates) using `meraki.templates.devices`.

Templates are either of type `model` (inline `configuration`, where every string value is rendered as a template) or of type `file` (a template file referenced by `file`, whose content must be provided via `file_templates`, rendered and decoded as YAML).

A template can inherit from other templates of the same kind (network or device) by listing them in its own `templates` attribute, where later parents take precedence. The templates referenced by a network or device are expanded with the templates they inherit from, and every template is applied once, in an order that keeps the order of the referenced templates and of the parents of every template, with parents applied before the templates inheriting from them (C3 linearization). If no such order exists, e.g. because a template is referenced after a template inheriting from it, or two templates list the same parents in a different order, an error is returned. Inheritance cycles and references to unknown parent templates are an error as well. Like other template errors, these errors only occur for templates that are used. `templates` and `variables` within the `configuration` of a template (or the content of a file template) are ignored, use the `templates` and `variables` attributes of the template instead.

A template can define default values for template variables in its own `variables` attribute. The default variables of all applied templates (including inherited ones) are merged in application order, so that a template overrides the defaults of its parents and of templates applied before it. Default variable values are not rendered as templates.

The following variables are available in templates, in increasing order of precedence:

- Network templates: `GLOBAL` (the `meraki` section of the merged model), the default variables of the applied network templates and the network's `variables`.
- Device templates: `GLOBAL`, the default variables of the network's templates, the default variables of the applied device templates, the network's `variables` and the device's `variables`.

The `variables` of a rendered network include the default variables of its templates. The `variables` of a rendered device include the default variables of its templates that are not overridden by the network's `variables`, so that the variables used for the device templates are always the rendered network `variables` merged with the rendered device `variables`.

Only template content is rendered, `${}` expressions in the regular configuration are left untouched. Returns an error if the same attribute is a different kind of value (map, list, or scalar) in a template and in the configuration.

The result contains the rendered model with `!env` tags preserved (`raw`), the rendered model with `!env` tags resolved (`resolved`) and the merged default values (`defaults`). Variables with `!env` tags can be used within strings (e.g. `Bearer ${token}`): they are resolved in `resolved` and kept unresolved in `raw`. In `raw`, a value consisting only of an `!env` tag is kept as `!env VAR` and written as a YAML tag by `yaml_encode`, so that YAML loaders with `!env` support (e.g. `nac-validate`, `nac-test`) resolve it. A tag used within a string is kept as text (e.g. `Bearer !env TOKEN`), which these tools do not resolve. If such a value needs to be resolved there, use a tag for the whole value instead (e.g. an environment variable containing `Bearer ...`). The `meraki.templates` section is not included in the rendered model.

~> This function is intended for use within the [Network as Code](https://netascode.cisco.com/) Terraform modules and is not intended for standalone use.

## Template Functions

The following functions are available inside `${}` template expressions in model and file templates:

**Numeric:** `abs`, `ceil`, `floor`, `log`, `max`, `min`, `parseint`, `pow`, `signum`, `sum`

**String:** `chomp`, `endswith`, `format`, `formatlist`, `indent`, `join`, `lower`, `regex`, `regexall`, `regexreplace`, `replace`, `sort`, `split`, `startswith`, `strcontains`, `strlen`, `substr`, `title`, `trim`, `trimprefix`, `trimsuffix`, `trimspace`, `upper`

**Collection:** `chunklist`, `coalesce`, `coalescelist`, `compact`, `concat`, `contains`, `distinct`, `element`, `flatten`, `index`, `keys`, `length`, `lookup`, `merge`, `one`, `range`, `reverse`, `setintersection`, `setproduct`, `setsubtract`, `setunion`, `slice`, `values`, `zipmap`

**Type Conversion:** `tobool`, `tonumber`, `tostring`

**Encoding:** `base64decode`, `base64encode`, `csvdecode`, `jsondecode`, `jsonencode`

**Date/Time:** `formatdate`, `timeadd`

**Boolean:** `alltrue`, `anytrue`

**Error Handling:** `try`, `can`, `fail`

`fail(message)` stops rendering with the message as error, e.g. `${contains(vlans, vlan) ? vlan : fail("VLAN ${vlan} is not defined")}`. Only the selected branch of a conditional (or `%{ if }` directive) is evaluated, and `try` and `can` catch the error.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    utils = {
      source = "netascode/utils"
    }
  }
}

provider "utils" {}

locals {
  model = {
    meraki = {
      templates = {
        networks = [
          {
            name = "branch"
            type = "model"
            configuration = {
              time_zone     = "Europe/Berlin"
              notes         = "Branch $${site_id}"
              product_types = ["appliance", "switch"]
            }
          }
        ]
        devices = [
          {
            name = "switch"
            type = "model"
            configuration = {
              address = "$${address}"
              tags    = ["$${role}"]
            }
          }
        ]
      }
      domains = [
        {
          name = "EMEA"
          organizations = [
            {
              name = "Org1"
              networks = [
                {
                  name      = "Branch1"
                  templates = ["branch"]
                  variables = {
                    site_id = 1
                    address = "Main Street 1"
                  }
                  devices = [
                    {
                      serial    = "Q2XX-XXXX-XXXX"
                      name      = "SW1"
                      templates = ["switch"]
                      variables = {
                        role = "access"
                      }
                    }
                  ]
                }
              ]
            }
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  }

  result = provider::utils::render_meraki_model([], local.model, "", {})
}

# Fully rendered network including its devices
output "network" {
  value = local.result.resolved.meraki.domains[0].organizations[0].networks[0]
}

/*
network = {
  "devices" = [
    {
      "address"   = "Main Street 1"
      "name"      = "SW1"
      "serial"    = "Q2XX-XXXX-XXXX"
      "tags"      = ["access"]
      "templates" = ["switch"]
      "variables" = {
        "role" = "access"
      }
    },
  ]
  "name"          = "Branch1"
  "notes"         = "Branch 1"
  "product_types" = ["appliance", "switch"]
  "templates"     = ["branch"]
  "time_zone"     = "Europe/Berlin"
  "variables" = {
    "address" = "Main Street 1"
    "site_id" = 1
  }
}
*/
```

## Signature

<!-- signature generated by tfplugindocs -->
```text
render_meraki_model(yaml_strings list of string, model dynamic, defaults_yaml string, file_templates dynamic) object
```

## Arguments

<!-- arguments generated by tfplugindocs -->
1. `yaml_strings` (List of String) List of YAML strings to decode and merge into the base model.
1. `model` (Dynamic) HCL model variable to merge on top of the YAML strings.
1. `defaults_yaml` (String) Module defaults YAML string. User defaults from model override these.
1. `file_templates` (Dynamic) Map of file path to pre-read file content for file-type templates.
